profile.campus: Lithia Springs, Douglas County, Georgia (Google's original Atlanta-metro data center campus, present since 2003)
profile.address: Switch Way, Mableton, Douglas County, Georgia, 30122
profile.reading: This is Google's original Georgia data center campus in Lithia Springs, Douglas County, in the Atlanta metro, where OpenStreetMap tags date Google's presence to 2003, among the company's earliest self-built US data center sites alongside The Dalles, Oregon. Google's initial building on the site totaled roughly 500,000 square feet, and in 2015 the company announced a $300 million expansion to add a second, adjacent building, with construction beginning that summer and completion targeted for 2016; Google said it already employed more than 350 people at the Douglas County campus at the time of that announcement, with the expansion expected to add at least 25 more data center jobs initially. Local and Georgia state officials provided tax incentives to attract the expansion, consistent with the state's broader push to draw hyperscale data center investment, and Google cited the project alongside a separate Singapore expansion announced the same day as evidence of its accelerating global infrastructure build-out. Google reported that its Georgia operations helped generate $2.76 billion of economic activity for roughly 62,000 Georgia businesses in 2014, a period corresponding to the run-up to the second-building announcement. Google has since made a far larger Georgia commitment through a separate, newer project: in April 2026 the company revealed itself as the developer behind the previously unnamed "Project Pegasus," an $8 billion data center campus retrofitting a 600,000-square-foot industrial building in LaGrange, roughly 70 miles southwest of Atlanta, which Google has described as complementing rather than replacing its original Douglas County operations. Google's data center locations page does not publish current square footage or MW capacity for the Douglas County campus specifically, so this registry records the 500,000-square-foot original building figure and the 2015 expansion investment as the best available operator-adjacent figures rather than current totals.

reading.body:
Google's Douglas County campus in Lithia Springs is the company's original Georgia data center investment, with roots dating to 2003, and represents an early bet on Atlanta-metro hyperscale capacity alongside the company's contemporaneous builds in Oregon. The original building totaled 500,000 square feet, and a $300 million second building, announced in 2015 and completed around 2016, expanded the campus footprint. Google does not publish current combined capacity or megawatt figures for this site.

The campus sits in Georgia's now-mature hyperscale data center market, where it ranks fifth among facilities with published capacity specifications, though thirty-three mapped facilities exist across the state and only four report megawatt figures publicly. Georgia's total published hyperscale capacity is 66.3 MW, a metric that understates actual deployment and reflects Google's broader preference for not disclosing individual campus figures.

Google has since made a far larger commitment to Georgia through Project Pegasus, an $8 billion campus retrofit in LaGrange announced in April 2026 and described by the company as complementing rather than replacing Douglas County operations. The persistence of this original site after more than two decades, and its designation as complementary rather than obsolete, suggests it retains operational value within Google's Georgia infrastructure strategy, though without published megawatt or current occupancy figures, its specific role in the company's AI training or serving footprint cannot be determined from public data.
